behavior_class_name: Backdoor Persistence Service Foothold Behavior Class
description: Registers a Windows service named A06_2_Persistent_Service with automatic startup behavior. The service runs under the Windows Service Control Manager, monitors active user sessions, impersonates the logged-on user, launches a user-session instance of itself with a launcher argument, and then uses a timer-based watchdog loop to start and maintain a benign sample application in the interactive user session.

persistent_service.role: self-installs as an auto-start Windows service, registers service control handlers, monitors user sessions, impersonates the active user, launches a user-session launcher instance, and maintains watchdog logic

service_header.role: defines service name, launcher argument, window class name, timer identifier, and service function prototypes

sample_payload.role: benign user-session payload launched and monitored by the service watchdog; writes periodic status messages to a log file

persistent_service: CreateProcessW used to launch target payload

service: A06_2_Persistent_Service is registered with the Service Control Manager
service process starts under the Windows service framework
service responds to stop, shutdown, and session-change control events
registry: Path value is written under HKLM\SOFTWARE\A06_2_Persistent_Service
process: A06_2_persistent_service.exe runs as the service process
service obtains or attempts to obtain active user token
service launches a user-session instance of A06_2_persistent_service.exe with ServiceIsLauncher argument
launcher instance creates a window/message-loop context
launcher checks for A06_2_SampleApp.exe using process enumeration
launcher starts A06_2_SampleApp.exe if it is not already running
A06_2_SampleApp.exe continues running in a loop
file_system: payload log contains periodic alive/beacon messages
host: services.msc or sc.exe can show A06_2_Persistent_Service
Procmon may record service creation and registry configuration activity
Sysmon may record service installation if configured
Sysmon or Procmon may record CreateProcessAsUserW launching the user-session launcher
Sysmon or Procmon may record A06_2_SampleApp.exe process creation
Task Manager may show the sample payload running in the logged-on user session
network: no HTTP or HTTPS traffic is required
no TCP command channel is opened

code_placement: Service installation, SCM registration, service lifecycle handling, registry configuration, WTS session enumeration, token duplication, impersonation, and user-session launcher creation are implemented in A06_2_persistent_service.exe. Watchdog process monitoring and payload launch logic are implemented in the launcher execution path of the same executable. Periodic benign payload logging is implemented in A06_2_SampleApp.exe.
execution_trigger: The installer executable is manually executed first. If not launched by the Service Control Manager, it performs self-installation as an auto-start service. The service then starts at boot or when started manually, launches a user-session watchdog when an active user session is available, and the watchdog starts the sample payload if it is not already running.
execution_target: Windows Service Control Manager, HKLM service configuration state, HKLM\SOFTWARE\A06_2_Persistent_Service configuration key, and controlled payload at C:\Users\Public\A06_2_SampleApp.exe
semantic_meaning: Demonstrates service-based persistence in which a durable auto-start Windows service acts as a watchdog and session bridge. The service persists across reboot, monitors user logon/session state, impersonates the active user, starts a user-session launcher, and maintains execution of a benign payload process.

mitre_attack_mapping.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service

related_techniques.relationship: conceptually related because execution is coordinated with user logon/session availability

control_notes.payload_effect: maintains a benign user-session sample application that writes periodic status logs

success_conditions: A06_2_persistent_service.exe is executed with administrative privileges
service creates or opens HKLM\SOFTWARE\A06_2_Persistent_Service
service writes Path value pointing to C:\Users\Public\A06_2_SampleApp.exe
A06_2_Persistent_Service is registered with the Service Control Manager
service startup type is configured as automatic
service starts successfully
service transitions to SERVICE_RUNNING
service writes entries to C:\Users\Public\A06_2_Persistent_Service_log.txt
an active user session is detected
service obtains the active user token using WTSQueryUserToken
service duplicates the token using DuplicateTokenEx
service creates a user environment block
service launches a user-session launcher instance using CreateProcessAsUserW
launcher instance starts with ServiceIsLauncher argument
launcher creates Local\A06_2_Launcher_Instance_Mutex
launcher reads target payload path from HKLM\SOFTWARE\A06_2_Persistent_Service\Path
launcher checks whether A06_2_SampleApp.exe is already running
launcher starts C:\Users\Public\A06_2_SampleApp.exe if not running
A06_2_SampleApp.exe writes initialization message to C:\Users\Public\A06_2_Persistent_Service_SampleApp_log.txt
A06_2_SampleApp.exe writes periodic alive/beacon log messages every five seconds
no network traffic or secondary payload download occurs
